To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of CWT with TOS merges two worlds into a time–bifequency domain that conveys information on non-stationarity and nonlinearity.
the CWT/TOS combination provides a new time–bifrequence domain that offers a new means for nonlinear analysis of wheeze sounds and dynamic EEG-based characterization of pain.

the continuous wavelet transformation combined with higher-order spectrum (CWT/HOS) is an innovative tool for the analysis of biomedical signals and that this combination can be applied in the analysis of wheezes and EEG signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two types of biomedical signal analysis: (1) wheeze analysis and (2) EEG-based pain analysis.
the application of the CWT/TOS method to two types of biomedical signal analysis, that is, (i) wheeze analysis and (ii) EEG-based pain characterization.
the development and application of a CWT/Tos field for the analysis of wheezes and EEG-based pain.

the CWT/TOS method can be considered an effective and reliable tool to characterize and classify wheeze sounds and pain states.
CWT/TOS is a novel and promising method for wheezes and pain detection and characterization.
the CWT/TOS is a promising method that can be utilized in the analysis of various signals and systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CWT/TOS combination provides a novel tool for the time–scale characterization of biomedical signals.

the combination of continuous wavelet transform with higher-order spectrum is a very useful tool to analyze the non-stationary, non-Gaussian and nonlinear biomedical signals, such as wheezes, and to characterize the pain based on EEG.
the CWT/TOS method can be used to detect the nonlinearities of biomedical signals, which are not detectable by other methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CWT and HOS can be used in conjunction to create a new time–bifreqeuncy domain for the representation of biomedical signals, which can be used for the analysis of their nonlinear characteristics.
the CWT/TOS combination can be applied in the fields of biomedical signal analysis and processing, and in the fields of signal processing in general, to offer a new means of analysis.

the CWT/TOS is a powerful tool for analyzing biomedical signals, such as wheezes and EEG signals, and it offers a time–biparametric domain for the analysis of the nonlinearity, non-Gaussianness and non-stationarity of the examined signals.
